html:
SMTO-LLM-0001 — Model request timed out

GUID: 93c20c49-a89a-4920-a48f-5a7cc051bcff
Slug: llm-request-timeout
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO waited for the model to answer, but no complete answer arrived within the time limit, so it stopped waiting. Steps that already finished in this task stay done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card and select Check saved model. This shows whether the model service answers at all, which separates a slow model from a stuck or broken one.
  2. If the check fails, ask the person who runs the model service to make sure it's running and not overloaded. A stalled or overloaded service causes the same timeout, and a longer limit won't fix it.
  3. If the check works but big requests are slow, open Limits and recovery on that card, raise Request timeout (in seconds), and select Save Main. A larger limit gives a slow but healthy model enough time to finish.
  4. Start a new task to use the new limit. Don't redo steps the earlier task already finished. A resumed task keeps the time limit it started with, and finished steps have already taken effect.

What success looks like

  • A new task receives a complete answer from the model without timing out.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model service. Don't change the command time limit for shell commands; it doesn't control how long SMTO waits for the model.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SMTO reached the model request / stream-read timeout without a complete response; the limit applies per connection or read, not to total generation time.

What this means

  • A connection or read exceeded its allowed wait. This limit can apply to one part of a stream, so it does not necessarily measure the total time spent generating. The timeout alone cannot distinguish slow generation, an interrupted connection or a stalled provider. Earlier completed tool operations keep their receipts.

Why this can happen

  • The configured connection or stream-read wait expired. A slow response and a connection that stopped delivering data can both reach this limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the effective request timeout with the recorded stream phase and time to first event, when available. A failure before the first event differs from a pause between later events.
  • Ask the provider operator to check service health and logs at the request time. If successful comparable requests need longer, a longer wait is a diagnostic test; if progress stopped, investigate the provider or connection.

How to fix it

  • Check provider health and the recorded request phase (Technical details show the effective timeout and stream timing). If comparable requests legitimately need longer, raise Request timeout (seconds) in the Limits and recovery section on the role's card in Settings › Setup › Model routing (1-1800 s) and start a new task; a resumed task keeps its saved timeout. The shell command timeout does not govern model requests.
  • Check provider health and the recorded request phase. If comparable requests need longer, adjust Mission Control → Model Configuration → Model request / stream-read timeout (seconds) for a new task. Resume keeps its saved timeout.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Request Timeout: model-configuration / llm_timeout_seconds. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A new task captures the intended timeout and receives a complete model response without reaching that wait limit.

What not to do

  • Do not change the foreground shell execution timeout to repair a model request timeout.
  • Do not blindly replay earlier completed tool operations.

Technical notes

  • Transport timeout identifies a wait limit, not elapsed total generation time or provider health. Effective timing is captured for the request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0005 — A command ran too long and SMTO stopped it
  • SMTO-LLM-0037 — An older retry attempt ran out of time
  • SMTO-CTX-0001 — The AI model said your request was too long for it
  • SMTO-LLM-0015 — The model ran out of room before finishing its reply
